rationale: #940 / #941 (swift lane, full extent 554 files of swift-nio). `nonisolated(unsafe)` is newer than the pinned wasm (same species as `~Copyable` and `#assert`) and the failure cost the file its whole `class` HEADER: header+body landed in an ERROR node instead of a class_declaration, so no container symbol existed and every member it owns was orphaned (ownerName undefined). #940: recover the CONTAINER from the ERROR's token sequence — child[0] is the nominal keyword `class`, child[1] the recovery's own name — so members regain their owner (`contains`). #941 rides the same file: the convenience initializer BELOW the recovered range is a file-scope sibling whose symbol carries no owner, and the pre-fix `ownerName ?? name` fallback minted the symbol's OWN name as a target (`instantiates constructor -> constructor`, not a type in this vocabulary). SW-G says unresolvable stays silent, and an initializer delegation is never a `calls` edge (`init` is not a name in this vocabulary — constructors are literally `constructor`). The positive half: the resolvable delegation ABOVE the recovery point still builds the recovered container, and the member read in `read()` still resolves through the recovered ownership.
